This vignette walks through scoring a simulated affinity-purification experiment
with `saintexpress::run_saint()`. No native binary is involved — everything runs
in pure R.

## Simulate a small AP-MS experiment

We define two real baits (`BaitA`, `BaitB`) with two replicates each, plus two
controls. Six preys exist; `BaitA` enriches for `Prey1`/`Prey2` and `BaitB` for
`Prey3`/`Prey4`. The remaining preys are background.

```{r simulate}
simulate_si <- function(seed = 42, mode = c("spc", "int")) {
  mode <- match.arg(mode)
  set.seed(seed)
  preys  <- paste0("Prey", 1:6)
  baits  <- c("BaitA", "BaitA", "BaitB", "BaitB", "Ctrl1", "Ctrl2")
  ips    <- paste0("IP", seq_along(baits))
  cort   <- c("T", "T", "T", "T", "C", "C")

  # One row per IP x prey; recover the bait for each IP.
  grid <- expand.grid(ipId = ips, preyId = preys, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  grid$baitId <- baits[match(grid$ipId, ips)]

  # A prey is enriched ("signal") only for its true bait; everything else is background.
  signal <- (grid$baitId == "BaitA" & grid$preyId %in% c("Prey1", "Prey2")) |
            (grid$baitId == "BaitB" & grid$preyId %in% c("Prey3", "Prey4"))

  # Draw every quantity in one vectorized call.
  if (mode == "spc") {
    lambda <- ifelse(signal, ifelse(grid$baitId == "BaitA", 20, 15), 0.5)
    grid$quant <- stats::rpois(nrow(grid), lambda)
  } else {
    mu <- ifelse(signal, ifelse(grid$baitId == "BaitA", 1e7, 5e6), 1e4)
    grid$quant <- stats::rexp(nrow(grid), 1 / mu)
  }

  inter <- grid[grid$quant > 0, c("ipId", "baitId", "preyId", "quant")]
  rownames(inter) <- NULL
  list(
    inter = inter,
    prey  = data.frame(preyId = preys, preyLength = 500L, preyGeneId = preys,
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    bait  = data.frame(ipId = ips, baitId = baits, CorT = cort,
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  )
}

si_spc <- simulate_si(mode = "spc")
str(si_spc, max.level = 2)
```

## Validate the input tables

```{r validate}
saintexpress::validate_saint_input(si_spc)
```

## Spectral-count scoring

```{r score-spc}
scores_spc <- saintexpress::run_saint(si_spc, mode = "spc", optimizer = "base")
scores_spc[, c("Bait", "Prey", "AvgP", "BFDR", "SaintScore")]
```

The true interactors (`Prey1`/`Prey2` for `BaitA`, `Prey3`/`Prey4` for `BaitB`)
should land at the top of each bait by `AvgP`:

```{r top-hits-spc}
top_per_bait <- function(df) {
  df <- df[order(df$Bait, -df$AvgP), ]
  do.call(rbind, by(df, df$Bait, head, 2))
}
top_per_bait(scores_spc)[, c("Bait", "Prey", "AvgP", "BFDR")]
```

## Volcano plot

The `FoldChange` column summarizes enrichment over the estimated background.
We plot it as an effect-size coordinate (`EFC`, here `log2(FoldChange)`) against
the `BFDR` evidence coordinate.

```{r volcano-spc, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
plot_volcano <- function(scores, title) {
  volcano_data <- scores
  volcano_data$EFC <- log2(volcano_data$FoldChange)
  volcano_data$neg_log10_bfdr <- -log10(pmax(volcano_data$BFDR, 1e-16))
  volcano_data$is_hit <- volcano_data$BFDR <= 0.05 & volcano_data$EFC >= 1

  plot(
    volcano_data$EFC,
    volcano_data$neg_log10_bfdr,
    pch = 19,
    col = ifelse(volcano_data$is_hit, "#B23A48", "#3D6F99"),
    xlab = "EFC (log2 fold change)",
    ylab = "-log10(BFDR)",
    main = title
  )
  abline(h = -log10(0.05), lty = 2, col = "grey40")
  abline(v = 1, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
  text(
    volcano_data$EFC,
    volcano_data$neg_log10_bfdr,
    labels = paste(volcano_data$Bait, volcano_data$Prey, sep = ":"),
    pos = 3,
    cex = 0.7
  )
}

plot_volcano(scores_spc, "SAINTexpress spectral-count volcano plot")
```

## Intensity scoring

The same simulator, with `mode = "int"`, produces continuous abundances.

```{r score-int}
si_int <- simulate_si(mode = "int")
scores_int <- saintexpress::run_saint(si_int, mode = "int", optimizer = "base")
top_per_bait(scores_int)[, c("Bait", "Prey", "AvgP", "BFDR")]
```

```{r volcano-int, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
plot_volcano(scores_int, "SAINTexpress intensity volcano plot")
```

## Data in SummarizedExperiment, QFeatures, ExpressionSet or anndataR

Quantitative proteomics data are often held in a container:
`SummarizedExperiment` or `QFeatures`, `ExpressionSet`, or `anndataR` when the
data are exchanged with Python. saintexpress depends on none of them. Each
container holds the same three pieces, and these are all `run_saint()` needs:

| Piece | SummarizedExperiment, QFeatures assay | ExpressionSet | anndataR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quantity matrix, preys x IPs | `assay(se)` | `exprs(eset)` | `t(adata$X)` |
| Sample table, one row per IP | `colData(se)` | `pData(eset)` | `adata$obs` |
| Feature table, one row per prey | `rowData(se)` | `fData(eset)` | `adata$var` |

We start from these three pieces for a small dummy experiment: two baits with
two IPs each and two control IPs. `P1` and `P2` bind `BaitA`, `P3` and `P4`
bind `BaitB`, `P5` and `P6` are background.

```{r container-pieces}
row_data <- data.frame(
  protein = c("P1", "P2", "P3", "P4", "P5", "P6"),
  gene = c("GENE1", "GENE2", "GENE3", "GENE4", "GENE5", "GENE6")
)
col_data <- data.frame(
  sample = c("IP1", "IP2", "IP3", "IP4", "IP5", "IP6"),
  bait = c("BaitA", "BaitA", "BaitB", "BaitB", "Ctrl", "Ctrl"),
  CorT = c("T", "T", "T", "T", "C", "C")
)
quant <- matrix(
  c(
    25, 22, 0, 1, 1, 0,
    18, 20, 1, 0, 0, 1,
    0, 1, 30, 27, 1, 0,
    1, 0, 15, 19, 0, 1,
    5, 6, 4, 5, 6, 5,
    2, NA, 3, 2, 2, 3
  ),
  nrow = 6,
  byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(row_data$protein, col_data$sample)
)
quant
```

The matrix goes to long format, one row per observed prey in an IP; `NA` and
`0` mean not observed. Together with the two tables this gives the SAINT input.

```{r container-to-saint}
inter <- as.data.frame(as.table(quant), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(inter) <- c("preyId", "ipId", "quant")
inter <- inter[!is.na(inter$quant) & inter$quant > 0, ]
inter$baitId <- col_data$bait[match(inter$ipId, col_data$sample)]

si_container <- list(
  inter = inter[, c("ipId", "baitId", "preyId", "quant")],
  prey = data.frame(preyId = row_data$protein, preyGeneId = row_data$gene),
  bait = data.frame(ipId = col_data$sample, baitId = col_data$bait, CorT = col_data$CorT)
)
scores_container <- saintexpress::run_saint(si_container, mode = "spc")
top_per_bait(scores_container)[, c("Bait", "Prey", "AvgP", "BFDR")]
```

The scores go back into a prey x bait matrix, which can be stored in any of
the containers, for example as an assay of a `SummarizedExperiment` with baits
as columns.

```{r saint-to-matrix}
tapply(scores_container$BFDR, scores_container[c("Prey", "Bait")], c)
```
